item.title: Qodana
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Qodana
https://www.jetbrains.com/qodana/
Code quality done right

Static code analysis by Qodana helps development teams follow agreed quality standards, and deliver readable, maintainable, and secure code. Powered by JetBrains.

* 2,500+ code checks
Use Qodana’s extensive inspection portfolio to spot performance issues, probable bugs, unused declarations, confusing code constructs, violations of naming and style conventions, and much more.

* Third-party license audit
Detect when third-party libraries and framework licenses used by your application are incompatible with your application’s license and cannot be used for a commercial project.

item.title: Deno
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Deno
https://deno.land
https://deno.town
https://github.com/denoland/deno

https://github.com/architect/architect

Deno is a brand new experimental JavaScript runtime and deno.town is a web based REPL with linting and code completion to help you explore and learn the API.
Why Deno?

It is very fast
Built in least privilege security
Standard esmodules
TypeScript, JSX and TSX dialects supported

How

AWS Lambda (and friends) by way of OpenJS Architect
Deployed continuously with begin.com (Note! We have not officially released Deno support. Keep reading if you are interested in that.)

item.title: Swagger 2
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Setting Up Swagger 2 with a Spring REST API
https://www.baeldung.com/swagger-2-documentation-for-spring-rest-api
Nowadays, front-end and back-end components often separate a web application. Usually, we expose APIs as a back-end component for the front-end component or third-party app integrations.

In such a scenario, it is essential to have proper specifications for the back-end APIs. At the same time, the API documentation should be informative, readable, and easy to follow.

Source: commit 9d1d48d in My-Notes.
